title: Canonical normalized truncation cocone
statement:
For a left exact additive functor between Grothendieck abelian categories and a bounded-below complex $K$, let $X$ be a type-zero exact couple whose $D$ objects and $\alpha$ maps agree with the truncation couple [def-sp-truncation-couple]. Put $H^n=H^n(RF K)$, define $j_{n,q}:D^{n-q,q}\to H^n$ by the inverse bridge followed by $H^n(RF(\tau_{\le q}K\to K))$, and let $c_n:D^{0,n}\to H^n$ be its component at $q=n$. Then $c_n$ is invertible, the transported $j_{n,n-p}$ form a cocone for $\alpha$ [def-sp-convergence], and for $p\ge0$ this cocone map is the incoming $p$-fold alpha iterate followed by $c_n$. No cohomological lower bound or identification of the $E,f,g$ data is required.

Exact Lean interface:
```lean
theorem truncation_abutment_cocone {A : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} A] [Abelian A] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v₁} A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w₁} A] {B : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} B] [Abelian B] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v₂} B] [HasDerivedCategory.{w₂} B] (F : A ⥤ B) [F.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits F] (K : CochainComplex.Plus A) (X : BigradedExactCouple B 0) (hD : X.D = TruncationCouple.D F K) (halpha : (∀ p q : ℤ, X.alpha p q = eqToHom (by rw [hD]) ≫ TruncationCouple.alpha F K p q ≫ eqToHom (by rw [hD]))) : ∃ (H : ℤ → B) (hH : H = fun n : ℤ ↦ (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor B n).obj (F.rightDerivedFunctor.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K.obj))) (j : ∀ n q : ℤ, X.D (n - q) q ⟶ H n) (c : ∀ n : ℤ, X.D 0 n ⟶ H n), (∀ n q : ℤ, j n q = eqToHom (by rw [hD]; unfold TruncationCouple.D; congr 1; omega) ≫ (TruncationCouple.bridgeIso F (TruncationCouple.truncation K q) n).inv ≫ (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor B n).map (F.rightDerivedFunctor.map (DerivedCategory.Q.map (K.obj.ιTruncLE q))) ≫ eqToHom (by rw [hH])) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, c n = eqToHom (by congr 1; omega) ≫ j n n) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, IsIso (c n)) ∧ (∀ n p : ℤ, X.alphaDiagonal n p ≫ eqToHom (by congr 1; omega) ≫ j n (n - p) = eqToHom (by congr 1; omega) ≫ j n (n - (p + 1))) ∧ (∀ (n p : ℤ) (hp : 0 ≤ p), eqToHom (by congr 1 <;> omega) ≫ j n (n - p) = X.incomingAlphaIter p.toNat 0 n ≫ c n)
```

proof.text:
Set H to the cohomology of RF(K), j to the inverse bridge followed by
RF of the truncation inclusion, and c to the degree-zero component of j.
The inclusion tau<=n K -> K induces an isomorphism in degree n by 05TC (2);
transport this isomorphism through the bridge to obtain invertibility of c.
For the cocone equation, substitute the definition of alpha. The adjacent
bridge and inverse bridge cancel. Functoriality reduces the result to the
transition followed by the truncation inclusion being the preceding inclusion.
Iterate this equation p times for p>=0. At p=0 the normalization is the
definition of c; the successor step uses the incoming-alpha recursion.
Integer transports respect these compositions by proof irrelevance.
